name: Shree Nathji Haveli
description:
An old Vaishnavite temple of Pushtimarg heritage where seva is offered to Govardhan Nathji (a form of Shri Krishna) and several other forms of Krishna.
Darshan:
Mangala - 7:30 am
Rajbhog - 11:30 am
Bhog-Arti - 5:30 pm
Shayan - 7 pm
The idol is 200+ years old and was retrieved from British antiquity looters in 1850s by Goswami Shri Krishnajivanji Maharaj and brought to Mumbai where it resided in Mota Mandir Mumbai for around 45 years.

The deity was then brought to Dahisar in 1995 with great joy and splendour at the request of the community of Vaishnavas in Dahisar.

Today, the temple celebrates more than fifty festivals in any given year. Prasadam distribution and satsang sessions for various age groups are held every day.

featured_reviews.review_text: Nestled in a small street of Kanderpada away from the busy hustle-bustle of Borivali / Dahisar is a sweet petit gate-frame [No-gate] that opens to a staircase that goes up a hill to a huge rock [Shown in my shared pics]. It's a perfect retreat for those seeking spiritual solace, historical insight, or simply a connection with nature.

There is plenty of parking space for visitors as well.

Vitthal Rakhumai Mandir, Dadar is a beautiful and spiritually enriching place that reflects the true essence of devotion and tradition. The temple has a very peaceful and divine atmosphere, making it an ideal place for prayer and meditation. The idols of Lord Vitthal and Goddess Rakhumai are beautifully adorned, and the overall energy of the temple is very positive.

The temple premises are clean and well maintained. Daily aarti, bhajans, and rituals are performed with great devotion, creating a soulful experience for devotees. Despite being located in a busy area of Dadar, the temple offers a calm and serene environment inside.

A must-visit temple for devotees of Lord Vitthal and anyone seeking spiritual peace and devotion. 🙏✨

featured_reviews.name: Kaushik Ghosh
featured_reviews.review_text: In one of the reviews you directly made a conclusion that someone is a Muslim and thats why they have such strict opinions about the temple. Mind you that it doesn't matter whether the person complaining is a Hindu or a Muslim. If the premise is creating nuisance then it is  nuisance. Love for God and spirituality should stem from within. Portraying it by flashy loud music during odd times of the day is disrespect to God and the people living nearby the temple premise. The temple can arrange it's prayer meets and day to day activities by peaceful means too. And before you judge me by my religion let me clarify I am a Hindu. To prove that I am a Hindu or possess love for God I do not need to seek validation by creating nuisance and destroying others peace of mind. Atleast have a little bit of concern for the hospital nearby and please curb your activities to minimal and also see to it that you do not block the road way as it is public property and not temple property . Har Har Mahadev 🙏🏻
